parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs national binary-document and entry-fraud screening with state birth-sex facilities, shelter and prison placement, a criminal bathroom-related exposure, and an upheld drag/impersonator ban carrying jail and a felony for repeat offences. No execution or organised visitor sweeps are documented, and courts, employment and marriage protections remain, but efficient institutions enforce hostile facility and custody rules. Universal facility/custody exposure plus criminal exposure for presentation places this below the 0.35 exclusion-only anchors; minor care, school and sports bans deepen family exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport policy, stopped X-marker processing, and 2025 cable directing refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility where documents raise reasonable doubt about sex.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements and limited waivers exist; passport policy is being litigated.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal, added evidence demands, or a fraud ground affecting future travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2026 state Act mandates transgender prison placement by sex assigned at birth and bans trans women from women's shelters; national corrections model includes hair cutting, hormone removal and substituted therapy.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented solitary, segregation or assault pattern for this state's trans prisoners; remedies and enforcement status of the 2026 Act are not sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for bathroom or performance offences can lead to birth-sex custody placement, compounding outing and safety risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State facilities must match sex assigned at birth; 2019 law defines transgender bathroom use matching identity as indecent exposure, though prosecutions are not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Warning-sign requirement was struck down in 2022; school bathroom ban remains in litigation; some municipalities have narrow public-employment ordinances.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National and state facility bans operate together; trespass or indecent-exposure theories can convert facility use into arrest risk.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned, new care was barred from July 2023 and existing care required withdrawn by March 2024; Supreme Court upheld the ban in June 2025.
care_services.protection: Adult visitor care access is not documented as banned; emergency care practice is not documented.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor or parent seeking continuity of care faces denial and potential civil penalties for assisting care; adult exposure is less documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2023 adult-entertainment law criminalises male/female impersonators where a child could see them, up to 11 months 29 days first offence and 1-6 years felony second; upheld on appeal, Supreme Court declined review.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Law was initially held vague and overbroad; a district attorney threat against Pride was enjoined; a separate suit remains ongoing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Ambiguous application to transgender presentation creates arrest and prosecution risk, especially for performers or visibly gender-nonconforming visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors face care bans, birth-sex school sports and bathrooms litigation, mandatory teacher reporting of name/pronoun requests to parents, and national investigation of schools for social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: School bathroom and sports litigation remains unresolved; no final disposition is sourced.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor risks outing to authorities or family contacts, denied care, and facility exclusion; guardians risk civil penalties for assisting prohibited care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Historical reporting described police and legal officials turning a blind eye to assaults and LGBTQ people being refused service and beaten; gay/trans panic defence remains available.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; a 2019 state prosecutor opinion allowed gender-based enhancement, but state hate-crime statute does not list gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence-rate figure is described as an undercount floor and, per rubric, is not used as prevalence evidence; documented tolerance gaps limit recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State lacks statewide employment, housing and public-accommodation protections; local ordinances cover public employment only and are preempted for private employers.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment ruling, marriage recognition, civil-liberties litigation and some injunctions provide partial recourse; several national orders have been blocked.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts also uphold hostile care and drag laws, so legal effectiveness does not mitigate the operative facility, custody and criminal exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar state exclusion and weak remedy, but this case is lower (less safe): Vellandra centres on entry denial without imprisonment, whereas here bathroom, drag and birth-sex custody rules create documented jail exposure.

This case is higher (safer) than 0.25-C because birth-sex prison placement is mandated but frequent custodial assault and slow safety petitions are not documented for this state; criminal facility and performance laws still pull it well below 0.35.

0.55-C involves partial ward denial with ethics remedies and no detention pathway; here facility exclusion is linked to criminalisation, prison placement and an upheld impersonator felony, making the operative exposure materially harsher.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: national document and entry screening can flag mismatch, state law then governs facilities, shelters and custody by birth sex, and criminal provisions can punish bathroom use or impersonation. Protections from national courts, employment law and marriage recognition operate in separate spheres and do not pre-empt those exposures. No lethal pathway is documented, but imprisonment, permanent immigration consequences, denied minor care and birth-sex custody are credible. That combination places the rating in the high-risk range, above custodial-violence regimes but below exclusion-only regimes.
